chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I accept work in which there is goldsmithing and engraving, and I stipulate with the engraver according to his condition. When the accounting is done between me and him, I take from him what was stipulated.' He said, 'Then, with his good pleasure.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on partnering with an engraver for mixed goldsmithing and engraving work in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on leases (Ijarat) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of mixed-skill partnerships, specifically between a goldsmith and an engraver, where the craftsman bears the risk of settling accounts with the subcontractor. Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmation 'la ba'sa' (there is no objection) highlights the flexibility in commercial contracts within Shia jurisprudence, provided the financial settlement is mutually agreed upon and executed with goodwill ('bitayb nafs'). This ruling underscores the principle that professional collaboration is valid as long as the terms of engagement and compensation are clear and consensual.
